analysis.title: GREED & fear: Election rout pending and credit tremors
key_insights: Christopher Wood argues the Conference Board consumer confidence index points to a Republican rout in the mid-term elections. The index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September, the lowest since April 2014, vs consensus of 89.0.

US equities have ignored rising bond yields and geopolitical tension because of strong earnings growth from the AI capex cycle. LSEG I/B/E/S consensus as of 25 September has S&P500 3Q26 earnings up 30.2% YoY, vs 16.1% expected last October.

IT sector 3Q26 earnings growth is forecast at 65.1% YoY (22.3% a year ago). Semiconductors are forecast at 131.7% and semiconductor materials & equipment at 68.9%. All 12 IT sub-industries have higher forecasts than a year ago.

The 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields, at 5.34% and 5.69%, hit their highest levels since April 2002 and May 2002 respectively. The report says this reconfirms its view since March 2020 that G7 bonds are in a structural bear market after a 39-year bull market.
The 2-year Treasury yield peaked at 4.96% this week, 108bp above the midpoint of the fed funds rate. The report reads this as a sign more rate hikes are coming.

The bond sell-off has lifted volatility and credit spreads. The MOVE index is almost back to its level when the US-Israel attack on Iran was launched, and US high-yield spreads have begun to widen. The report treats MOVE as more important than VIX because bonds are collateral in a leveraged system.
The report says the real credit damage is in private credit, which cannot be seen on a mark-to-market basis.

A counter-trend bond rally can happen after the 10-year yield rose 82bp last quarter, but the report has no interest in playing it. It adds that a 75bp fed funds hike by Kevin Warsh this year could be positive for the long end.

Core PCE rose 3.0% YoY in August vs 3.3% consensus, and annual revisions cut core PCE by 0.3-0.4ppt in the previous three months. Money markets now discount 30bp of further hikes by year-end, down from 52bp in mid-September.
Mortgage rates are at 7.3% and the MBA mortgage applications index fell 6% WoW in the week ended 25 September and is down 37% YoY. The report calls this a political negative for the White House.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll (17-20 September) shows 62% of Americans disapprove of US military strikes on Iran and 67% disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy.
The report names three dominant investor issues: the duration and returns of the AI capex cycle, the structural bear market in G7 government bonds, and shifting geopolitics.

On US-Iran negotiations, the report believes Iran will only negotiate on the basis of the June MOU signed in Versailles and does not buy the view that economic pressure will force Tehran to be more accommodative. China is the key variable as the only country with leverage over Tehran.

China announced property support. This includes a new mortgage interest subsidy of 1 percentage point annualised on up to Rmb1m of mortgages for up to five years, for first-time buyers of units up to 120sqm and Rmb1.5m or less. The MSCI China Property Index is up only 2.6% since the announcement.

China household loans fell 1.6% YoY in August, with a record Rmb1.03tn decline in the first eight months of 2026. The new subsidy is the first central government nationwide measure to support housing demand.

EM local currency government bonds have beaten G7 government bonds by 59% since March 2020 in USD terms. The report's global sovereign bond portfolio (local currency, 6.97% average yield) has beaten the Bloomberg G7 index by 73.5% since 26 March 2020. It rose 2.9% last quarter vs a 2.7% G7 decline, and is up 4.8% YTD vs a 4.2% G7 decline.

Quarterly portfolio review: the Asia ex-Japan portfolio rose 3.2% last quarter vs a 0.2% decline in the MSCI AC Asia ex-Japan, but is up 13.6% YTD vs 26.0% for the benchmark due to its underweight in major semiconductor stocks. TSMC, Samsung Electronics and Hynix make up 33.5% of the benchmark.

The Japan portfolio rose 10.2% last quarter vs 7.4% for the Topix and is up 21.7% YTD vs 22.8%. The Japan dividend income portfolio rose 17.4% in yen last quarter and is up 28.0% YTD, with a 3.3% average forward yield.
The China portfolio fell 5.1% last quarter and 12.2% YTD. The India portfolio fell 2.2% last quarter vs a 5.5% decline for MSCI India, and fell 7.2% YTD vs a 14.7% decline for the index.
The global long-only portfolio rose 5.3% last quarter vs 1.7% for MSCI AC World, but is up 10.3% YTD vs 13.4%. The international long-only portfolio is up 20.1% YTD vs 14.7%.

market_movers.rationale: Idemitsu Kosan is listed as BUY in the report's other-companies-mentioned section. It is a holding in the Japan dividend income portfolio, with a 2.7% forward yield.

sector_views.rationale: IT has the second-highest forecast 3Q26 earnings growth at 65.1% YoY, driven by the AI capex cycle. This is the reason US equities have ignored rising yields.

earnings_insights: LSEG I/B/E/S consensus as of 25 September: S&P500 3Q26 earnings expected +30.2% YoY, vs +16.1% expected as of last October. This is a consensus estimate, not a reported figure.

trade_ideas.description: Hold a local-currency EM government bond portfolio instead of G7 government bonds: China renminbi 5-year (20%), India rupee 15-year (25%), Singapore dollar 10-year (25%), Brazil real 10-year (30%).
trade_ideas.rationale: G7 bonds are in a structural bear market, and the portfolio has outperformed the G7 index by 73.5% since 26 March 2020.

risk_factors: Rising bond yields and a structural bear market in G7 government bonds.
A hawkish new Federal Reserve under Kevin Warsh and possible further rate hikes.
Private credit stress that is not visible on a mark-to-market basis, plus widening high-yield spreads.
Duration of the AI capex cycle and whether spending earns adequate returns.
Geopolitical tension tied to the US-Iran conflict.
A Republican rout in the mid-term elections.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots the Conference Board US Consumer Confidence Index at 81.9 in September 2026, the lowest since April 2014.
Exhibit 3 plots US 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields at 5.34% and 5.69%, the highest since April 2002 and May 2002.
Exhibit 4 plots the US 2-year Treasury yield at a 4.96% peak against the fed funds midpoint, 108bp below.
Exhibit 7 plots US core PCE inflation, revised down 0.3-0.4ppt in the previous three months to 3.0% YoY in July.
Exhibit 8 plots the MBA mortgage applications index, down 37% YoY.

Exhibit 12 lists the global sovereign bond portfolio: China renminbi 5-year 1.40% yield (20% weight), India rupee 15-year 7.38% (25%), Singapore dollar 10-year 2.45% (25%), Brazil real 10-year 14.10% (30%), average yield 6.97%.
vol_and_positioning: The MOVE index is almost back at the level prevailing when the US-Israel attack on Iran was launched. The report considers MOVE more important than VIX.
US high-yield corporate spreads have begun to widen after the bond rout.
Sentiment indicators on Treasuries are assumed to be almost universally bearish, which sets up a possible counter-trend rally. The report does not intend to play it.
geopolitical: US-Iran negotiations: Iran sent its president and foreign minister to the UN General Assembly and says it will only negotiate on the basis of the MOU signed by Trump in Versailles in June.
The report notes the contrary narrative that economic pressure on Tehran will force it to be more accommodative, and rejects it because Iran has shown it can take a lot of pain.
China is the one country with leverage over Tehran. Xi Jinping skipped the UN General Assembly during his US state visit.
The US-Israel attack on Iran is the earlier event whose volatility level the MOVE index is now close to.
Polling: 62% of Americans disapprove of US military strikes on Iran (Reuters/Ipsos, 17-20 September).

tension_points.bull_case: A counter-trend bond rally can come at any time after the 82bp rise in the 10-year yield last quarter. Sentiment on Treasuries is bearish, and a 75bp Warsh hike could help the long end. Core PCE came in at 3.0% vs 3.3% consensus, and hike pricing fell to 30bp from 52bp.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10-year at 5.34% and 30-year at 5.69% are the highest since 2002. The report holds that G7 bonds are in a structural bear market, with the 2-year at 4.96% pointing to more hikes. MOVE and high-yield spreads are rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 75bp fed funds rate rise by Warsh this year could turn the long end positive, per the report.
